On the data: earlier drafts of this brief supplied real, named institutions and governments with specific exposure figures, three times, under three different labels. None of it was used — every scenario below runs on fictional counterparties built to the same shapes.
01 · Landing page

Relationships, before any number

/ is a single search box. Typing an entity, counterparty, country, or theme resolves it and shows what it's connected to — a PFE figure or a priority label never appears before a relationship does.

02 · Search result

Search → top related → inspector → exposure

Searching an entity surfaces its top five relationships first. Clicking Inspect opens the Relationship Inspector — the correlation components and the typed structural path side by side. Business exposure, when any exists, is the last thing on the page.

03 · Score decomposition

The relatedness score, decomposed exactly

Feedback from an earlier review: a single composite number doesn't explain itself. Each relationship pair now returns an exact waterfall — component value × renormalized weight, summed to the final score, with unavailable components shown as excluded rather than silently zeroed. Not an estimate: the bars reconcile to the score bit-for-bit.

04 · Triage

Inbox: five things, not a dashboard

The former Daily Review, demoted from default landing page to a secondary route. No KPI card row — filters are plain text links — and the table caps at five rows by the same priority logic used everywhere else, not a separate model.

05 · Counterparty detail

Three tabs, not seven sections

Counterparty 360 used to be a single scroll through seven stages. It's now three tabs — Relationships, Exposure & Controls, Decision — covering the same ground with a fraction of the scroll.

06 · Event analysis

The business answer first, the method behind a toggle

Parsing a narrative leads with classification, transmission path, and a five-row decision table. Entity/theme extraction, and the two internal ranking modes (bounded traversal vs. personalized PageRank), collapse behind one How was this derived? control.

07 · Governance

Control Exceptions: 14 columns down to 6

Breaches & Actions is now Control Exceptions — Subject, Control, Exception, Age, Owner, Action. Everything else (legal entity, product, limit value, SLA, root cause) moved into an expandable row.

Full source, the CCR decision-workflow writeup, and the test suite are on GitHub. Run locally with a FastAPI backend and a Vite/React frontend — no external services required in offline deterministic mode.
